subject: Observed heartbeat anomalies and elevated response latency — customer advisory

Subject: Observed heartbeat anomalies and elevated response latency — customer advisory

Hi Alice / Peregrine team,

Quick note to make you aware we observed an unusual pattern affecting a subset of hosted inference requests in the US-west region starting ~08:05 PST this morning. Symptoms we saw: elevated p95/p99 generation latencies (up to ~4.2s vs baseline ~220ms), a small fraction of 500/502 responses, and transient heartbeat-timeout traces in our edge telemetry.

What we did so far:
- Activated us-west routing fallback to adjacent pools at 08:18 PST to reduce customer impact.
- Applied a temporary request-throttling shim for long-running generation jobs to protect control plane.
- Opened an internal ops bridge and started root-cause triage.

Impact to you: we routed a portion of your traffic (token streams using route-id: peregrine-prod) to a secondary pool from 08:18–08:45 PST. You may have seen delayed responses or a few 503/502s during that window. We do not have evidence of data loss; requests were retried where applicable.

Ask: please confirm whether you observed user-visible failures beyond what I described (time windows, affected endpoints). If you have specific traces or request IDs, include them and we’ll prioritize those.

We’ll post updates to the incident page as we have them: https://status.redwood.inference.com/incidents/2028-01-17-heartbeat-anomaly

Attaching a short ops runbook excerpt for the temporary mitigation we applied (ops-runbook.pdf).

Sorry for the disruption — we recognize the impact and are treating it as high priority. I’ll follow up with a full postmortem link once available.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Observed heartbeat anomalies and elevated response latency — internal notes

Marissa / Sean — internal triage summary for the incident (short):

Timeline (UTC):
- 2028-01-17T16:05Z — first heartbeat anomaly detected by edge probes (elevated RTT + missing health-check acks on some nodes).
- 2028-01-17T16:12Z — partial routing fallback engaged for affected pools.
- 2028-01-17T16:18Z — mitigation throttle applied to long-running generation requests to prevent KV-cache thrash.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a combination of a kernel-level NIC firmware regression on a small number of US-west hosts + a workload spike that amplified KV cache eviction pressure. The NIC regression caused occasional packet bursts to be dropped, producing heartbeat gaps that looked like node unhealthiness; the router reacted and shifted traffic, which increased load on healthy pools and the cache eviction loop.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Ops: escalate affected host firmware to infra provider and schedule rolling firmware rollback where possible (assigned: infra-ops).
- Runtime: add temporary conservative KV-cache TTL for top-traffic models to reduce eviction frequency (assigned: runtime team, ETA 3h).
- CS/AE: notify affected customers with window and credit options; prepare postmortem draft.

I attached the runbook excerpt that Sean referenced and will share the postmortem draft in Drive once the technical write-up is ready.

Subject: Post-incident update and public status page link — 2028-01-17 heartbeat anomaly

Hi Alice and team,

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. We’ve posted a customer-facing incident summary and the full postmortem draft to the status page and our shared drive: https://status.redwood.inference.com/incidents/2028-01-17-heartbeat-anomaly

Summary highlights:
- Root cause: intermittent NIC firmware regression combined with amplified KV-cache eviction pressure under a traffic burst in the US-west pool.
- Impact window: 2028-01-17 08:05–08:45 PST for affected requests; residual elevated p95 for up to ~60 minutes as traffic rebalanced.
- Customer mitigation: we applied routing fallbacks and a short-term throttle, and we rolled back firmware on affected hosts where possible.
- What we’re doing next: conservative KV-cache TTL, improved preflight probes to avoid spurious unhealth signals, and a targeted firmware remediation plan with our infra provider.

We recognize the disruption and have applied a one-time account credit to Peregrine Analytics for the impacted window. If you would like a collaborator review of the postmortem before it’s finalized, I can set up a short call.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (internal draft).

Apologies again for the interruption — please reach out if you see anything in the postmortem that needs clarifying.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
